name: Hingol, Pakistan
summary: Active sedimentary mud volcanoes (Chandragup) and wind-carved badlands mirroring Acidalia Planitia's pitted cones.

radarView.source: Copernicus Data Space / CSA Open Data
radarView.caption: C-band SAR resolves wind-carved badland canyons and mud-volcano cone flanks across Hingol National Park.

name: Kharan Desert, Pakistan
summary: Dry, dusty, barren rocky gravel flats and sand sheets closely reproducing Gale Crater's ventifact plains.

name: Dasht-e Lut, Iran
summary: Hottest land surface measured by NASA MODIS, sculpted into parallel wind-carved kalut yardangs akin to Medusae Fossae.

name: Dalangtan / Qaidam Basin, China
summary: 2.7 km high-altitude hyper-arid evaporite basin rich in Mg-sulfates and wind-carved ridges — Earth's premier Meridiani twin.

radarView.caption: C-band SAR separates smooth Dalangtan magnesium-sulfate salt pans (dark) from wind-carved ridges (bright).

name: Samail Ophiolite, Oman
summary: Largest exposed oceanic mantle peridotite — olivine, serpentine, and carbonate veins mirroring Nili Fossae & Jezero.

name: Lonar Crater, India
summary: Earth's only known hypervelocity impact crater excavated into flood basalt — direct structural twin to Linné Crater.

radarView.instrument: JAXA ALOS-2 PALSAR-2 L-Band / CSA RCM
radarView.caption: Orbital SAR reveals the circular 1.88 km basaltic impact rim, upturned ejecta collar, and interior wall gullies.

name: Chagai / Koh-e-Taftan, Pakistan
summary: Hyper-arid, barren volcanic domes and rocky basaltic aprons — morphological match for the Marius Hills volcanic dome province.

name: Mount Suswa, Kenya
summary: Double-caldera shield volcano pierced by 40+ collapsed lava-tube skylights — premier terrestrial lab for lunar cave shelters.

name: Pinacate Volcanic Field, Mexico
summary: Official NASA Apollo 14 & 17 astronaut geology training site — maar craters, volcanic ash, and basaltic lava fields.

radarView.caption: Dual-polarization SAR differentiates rough basaltic aa lava flows from smooth pyroclastic cinder aprons at El Pinacate.

name: Teide / Las Cañadas, Tenerife
summary: Barren 2,180 m volcanic caldera above the cloud deck — active lunar rover autonomy and Apollo 15 highland slope analog.

radarView.caption: C-band SAR maps rough basaltic lava tongues and high-slope caldera walls used for European lunar rover trials.
